# Cleaning up the source tree

Status: design for 3.0, waiting for Xaymar's review. Nothing in the code changes with this document. The numbers are from
`main` at 8b21745 (26 Nov 2026).

The plan moves files into folders, gives them names that say what is in them, splits the files that hold several
unrelated things, and decides what file-local code looks like (the unnamed namespaces). Every step is a move or a split
without a change in behaviour, in small PRs that can be reviewed by looking at the rename list.

## What is wrong today

### Flat folders

| Folder | Files | Note |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `code_runtime/source` | 128 | Plus 68 generated files in `d3d11/`. 110k lines, of which 37k are generated (`shaders.inc`, `shaders_opengl.inc`, `smaa.inc`) |
| `code_compiler/source` | 37 | Lexer, parser, code generation, the driver and the Windows resources side by side; `ast/` has one file |
| `tools` | 45 | Fixture generators, benchmarks, shader generators, build scripts, the hook and the VS Code grammar in one list |
| `tests/suite` | 202 | Grouped only by file name prefix (`blitz3d_` 99, `graphics_` 40, `language_` 17, ...) |

In `code_runtime/source` the only grouping is the file name prefix, and the prefix does not mean one thing:
`graphics_` is used for the renderer, for the image codecs, for input, for the clipboard and for the window system.

`streams.h`, `load_pool.hpp`, `parallel.hpp`, `scene.hpp`); none of the compiler's 23 `.cpp` files has one.

### Unnamed namespaces

There are **128 unnamed namespaces in 85 files** (everything outside `third_party`), holding about 22,500 lines:
734 functions, 367 variables and 215 types. 75 are at file scope, 53 are nested inside a named namespace
(`namespace bb::gfx { namespace { ... } }`). Next to them there are 396 file-scope `static` functions in 47 files, and
24 files use both styles.

Why they are there: the C++ Core Guidelines (SF.22) recommend an unnamed namespace over `static` for file-local code,
and it is the only way to give a **type** internal linkage. Most of them were written that way by default. The nested
form exists so that the helpers can use the names of the enclosing namespace without qualifying them.

What they do that matters, and has to be kept: they keep same-named helpers of different files apart. 42 helper names
exist in more than one file's unnamed namespace, for example:

* `graphics_d3d11.cpp` and `graphics_opengl.cpp` share 15 of them (`record`, `play`, `keep`, `forget_recorded_calls`,
  `pipeline_for`, `build_pipeline`, `apply_bindings`, `image_of`, `view_of`, ...): the two immediate-mode backends have
  the same call-list machinery, written twice.
* `executable_path` in four `main.cpp`s, `usage`, `quote` and `find_userlibs` in two: the tools copy their helpers.
* `create_resources` in `graphics_gamma.cpp`, `graphics_hdr.cpp` and `graphics_smaa.cpp`; `read_node`/`read_mesh` in
  `b3d.cpp` and `model_3ds.cpp`; `u16`/`u32`, `put16`/`put32`, `lower`, `has_extension` in several.

If those became external symbols, the static library would define them twice (an ODR violation that the linker only
sometimes reports), and in the planned whole-runtime ThinLTO they would be exported from their module for nothing.

What they cost: debuggers, profilers and crash reports show `(anonymous namespace)::record` without saying which
backend; a test can't reach them; and the two styles side by side make it unclear what the rule is.

### Other smells

* **Hand-written prototypes instead of headers.** 125 `bb_` functions are declared by hand inside other `.c`/`.cpp`
  files (`gui_render.cpp` has 26, `system.cpp` 11, `sound.c` 10). `bb_runtime_error` is declared in 9 places,
  `bb_is_debug` in 8, `bb_graphics_idle` in 5. These are `extern "C"`, so nothing checks that a declaration matches
  the definition: a changed parameter type compiles and is wrong at run time.
* **Generated files next to the code.** `shaders.inc` (20,840 lines), `shaders_opengl.inc`, `smaa.inc` and the 68
  files of `d3d11/` are generated by `tools/generate_shaders.py`, `translate_shaders.py` and `generate_smaa.py`, and
  are committed into `code_runtime/source`, where searches and file lists hit them.
* **Copied helpers between the tools.** See above: blitzcc, blitz-format, blitz-tidy, blitz-lsp and blitz-recompiler
  each have their own `executable_path` and friends, although `code_tools` exists as the shared library.
* **Names that say nothing.** One-letter names outside of loop counters and coordinates are everywhere: as parameter
  names alone, `s` appears 189 times, `h` 166, `b` 125, `p` 78, `m` 73, `e` 61, `o` 59 (and more as locals, `k` among
  them). `s` is a surface in the scene code, a string in the runtime, a stream in the file code and a state in the
  renderer. Function names do the same: `add`, `find`, `scan`, `convert`, `keep`, `play`, `record`, `release`, `lower`,
  `u16`, `put32`, `info_of`, `view_of` are file-local helpers whose name only makes sense with the file open.
* **Structures that grew.** `bb::gfx::state` (`graphics_internal.hpp`) has about 100 members, 21 of them `bool`s
  spread between pointers and floats; `bb::entity` (`scene.hpp`) has about 80, 13 `bool`s, with the data of every
  entity class (camera, light, mesh, sprite, terrain, listener) in one struct; `gadget` in the GUI 44; the `builder`s
  of the glTF and .x loaders 116 and 68. Members are in the order they were added, not by what uses them together,
  which costs padding and, for `entity`, cache lines in the loops over entities.
* **Test selection by file name.** `tests/test_selection.json` maps runtime files to test areas with regular
  expressions on file names (`graphics_(input|joystick|devices)`, `scene[a-z_0-9]*|animation...|graphics_scene3d`).
  Folders would make those rules one prefix each.

### code_compiler

```
code_compiler/source/

              runtime, the MinGW sysroot), build.cpp (compile and link), run.cpp, windows_resource.*
```

`driver/` is also where the runtime cache of the ThinLTO design goes (`runtime_cache.cpp`), instead of growing
`main.cpp` further.

### The tools and the rest

* `code_tools` becomes the one shared library for all executables, and gets the copied helpers (`executable_path`,
  `usage` formatting, `quote`, `find_userlibs`). blitzcc and blitz-recompiler link it too.
* `tools/` gets folders: `tools/build/` (build.cmake/.cmd/.sh, check_environment.py), `tools/generate/` (shaders,
  SMAA, D3D11 table, include keys, LSP help, VS Code grammar), `tools/fixtures/` (the `generate_*_fixtures.py` and
  `render_*` scripts), `tools/hooks/` (pre-commit.sh, install-hooks.sh). The `benchmark_*.bb/.py` files move to
  `benchmarks/`. `tools/wiki`, `tools/vscode` and `tools/smaa` stay.
* `tests/suite` stays flat for now: test names come from the file names and the known-failure lists and the test
  selection go by them. A move there renames tests, which is a change people see in CI and the known-failure lists, so
  it is left out of this plan unless Xaymar wants it.

## Naming rules

1. **The folder says the area, the file says the part.** No area prefix in a file name inside its folder:
   `gui/render.cpp`, not `gui/gui_render.cpp`.
2. **Translation units have unique base names in their target.** `.c`/`.cpp` files are what profilers, crash reports,
   object files and the ThinLTO cache name, so two `render.cpp` in one target are not allowed. Where a short name would
   repeat, it gets a qualifier (`gui/render.cpp` stays, `scene/render/` files are `record.cpp`, `culling.cpp`, ...).
   Headers may repeat (`internal.hpp` in each folder), because they are always included by path. A check in
   `tools/hooks/pre-commit.sh` and CI enforces it.
3. **Includes are written from the source root of the target**: `#include "graphics/internal.hpp"`, never
   `"../graphics/internal.hpp"`. Each target has exactly one private include folder, its `source/`.
4. **A file's first comment says what is in it**, and it is changed with the code (every file has one; see the list of
   files without one above).
5. **A file holds one area of the Blitz API or one internal subsystem.** When a file starts holding a second, the
   second gets its own file. As a guide, a hand-written file over ~1500 lines is reviewed for a split.
6. **Generated files live under a folder named for it** (`rhi/shaders/` here) and say at their top which tool made them,
   which they do already.
7. **Cross-file `bb_` functions are declared in a header**, never by hand in a `.c`/`.cpp`. `core/api.h` declares
   every `bb_` function that another runtime file calls (`bb_runtime_error`, `bb_is_debug`, `bb_graphics_idle`,
   `bb_set_buffer`, ...), and the file that defines one includes it, so the compiler checks both sides.

8. **Names say what a thing is.** One letter only for loop counters (`i`, `j`, `k` as a third counter) and for
   coordinates and components (`x`, `y`, `z`, `w`, `u`, `v`, `r`, `g`, `b`, `a`). Everything else is a word:
   `surface`, `entity`, `stream`, `brush`, not `s`, `e`, `b`. A function says what it does and to what:
   `append_png_chunk`, `read_u16_le`, `find_mouse_device`, not `add`, `u16`, `find`.
9. **Structures are grouped by use.** Members that are read together sit together; flags are packed into one place;
   data that only one kind of object needs is in its own struct (for `entity`: a camera, light, mesh, sprite, terrain
   part). Where a structure is hot, its layout is checked with a `static_assert` on its size.

## File-local code

Rule, for all C++ in the repository:

* **File-local functions and variables are `static`.** In C files that is already the only way.
* **File-local types get a unique name in the component's named namespace** (`bb::rhi::d3d11::recorded_call`,
  `bb::models::x::token`), where the namespace says whose they are. The backends already define their RHI calls in
  `bb::rhi::<backend>` (see `rhi_backend.hpp`); this extends it to their helpers.
* **No unnamed namespaces.** The rule replaces them; a check in the pre-commit hook and CI keeps new ones out.

Why this and not "everything into a named `detail` namespace": that would give the 734 helper functions external
linkage. The 42 repeated names would then be defined twice in `blitzrt.a`, the archive would export hundreds of symbols
that nobody outside the file uses, and every one of them would be a ThinLTO export, which stops the optimizer from
dropping or fully inlining it. `static` keeps internal linkage, reads the same in C and C++, and is greppable.

The one thing `static` can't do is make a type internal, hence the unique names in a named namespace. For a type that
is the same as having its own file's name in front of it, which is also what makes it readable in a debugger.

Where two files have the same helpers because they do the same thing (the D3D11 and OpenGL call lists, the three
`create_resources`, the copied tool helpers), the cleanup moves them into one shared place instead of renaming both
copies. Those are listed separately in the plan below because they are refactors, not moves.

## Interaction with whole-runtime ThinLTO (docs/Runtime-LTO.md)

* **Do the moves first.** The LTO design ships `runtime/source/` with a generated `manifest.txt` that lists every
  source with its flags and SHA-256, and caches objects per source. Moving files after it is in would change every
  cache key and the shipped tree a second time; moving them before means it is built on the final names.
* **The manifest and the shipped tree keep the folders.** `runtime/source/` mirrors `code_runtime/source/`, the
  manifest lists paths relative to it, and the cache's `objects/` mirrors them too (or rule 2 above makes a flat
  folder safe). The manifest is written from the CMake target, so it follows the moves by itself.
* **The inline C set has to keep working until LTO replaces it.** Today `code_compiler/CMakeLists.txt` lists the
  inline files by path and copies them flat into `runtime/inline/`, where they include each other by bare name. Two
  ways: keep every inline file and the headers they include in `core/` (the layout above does that), or copy the tree
  with its folders. The first one changes nothing for blitzcc and is the plan; `core/api.h` is added to the list.
* **`static` and LTO.** ThinLTO promotes an internal function that another module imports (renamed with a
  `.llvm.<hash>` suffix), so `static` does not stop cross-module inlining. It does keep the symbol out of the export
  list, which is what lets the linker drop it.
* **Files that stay native** (`memory_interpose.c`, the allocator part of `memory.cpp`) are named in the manifest
  by their new paths.

## Migration plan

Every PR in the plan:

* moves or splits, and changes nothing that a program can see. The test suite is the check; there is nothing to
  benchmark, except for the splits of hot files (`graphics_scene3d.cpp`, `scene_meshes.cpp`), which get one
  spacebattle/forest run on a physical machine to show that the split did not move anything that was inlined before.
* uses `git mv` in a commit of its own, with the include and CMake edits in the next commit, so the rename commit is
  100% similar and `git log --follow` and `git blame` keep the history. (The pre-commit hook rewrites the copyright
  header of a moved file; that keeps it above the rename threshold.)
* splits a file by `git mv` of the original to the biggest part and copying the rest out, so the biggest part keeps
  its history.
* updates `tests/test_selection.json`, `tests/ci/test_select.py`, `code_compiler/CMakeLists.txt`, the workflow paths,
  the tools that write into `code_runtime/source` and the docs that link to moved files, in the same PR.
* is one area, so that an open PR that touches another area rebases without conflicts. Open PRs rebase across a pure
  move without trouble (git's rename detection), but not across a split of the file they change, so splits wait for
  the PRs on that file.

### Phase 1: rules and checks (no moves)

1. This document.
2. The two checks (no unnamed namespace in new code, unique TU base names) in the pre-commit hook and CI, as warnings
   that list today's offenders, so nothing has to move for them to land.
3. `api.h` (in the flat folder for now, `core/api.h` after the moves): the cross-file `bb_` declarations, removing the 125
   hand-written ones. This is the only step in phase 1 that touches many files, and it can find real mismatches; any it
   finds are fixed in a commit of their own and named in the PR.
4. Fix the wrong and missing first comments (`userlib.c`, `graphics_streaming.cpp`, `graphics_presenter.cpp`,
   `rhi.hpp`, and the files with none).

### Phase 2: moves, one folder per PR

In this order, the areas with no open PR first:

| PR | Moves | Waits for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `rhi/shaders/` (generated files, the generators' output paths, the workflow check) | nothing |
| 2 | `files/`, `network/`, `recompiler/`, `kernels/` | nothing |
| 3 | `gui/` | nothing |
| 4 | `models/`, `collision/`, `physics/` | nothing |
| 5 | `codecs/`, `input/` | nothing |
| 6 | `core/`, `system/` (with the inline list in `code_compiler/CMakeLists.txt`) | nothing |
| 7 | `scene/` | #709 (`scene_meshes.cpp`, `scene.hpp`) |
| 8 | `graphics/`, `rhi/`, `rhi/<backend>/` | #646, #647, #723 |
| 9 | `audio/` | #717, #720, #722 |
| 10 | `code_compiler/source/{driver,frontend,codegen}` and `blitz_include/` | the audio PRs (`builtins.inc`, `all.bb`) |
| 11 | `tools/` folders and the benchmarks | nothing |

A pure move does not strictly have to wait for an open PR (it rebases across it), but waiting costs nothing and saves
the open PR a rebase it would have to explain.

### Phase 3: unnamed namespaces, one area per PR

Same order as phase 2, after the area has moved. In each PR: functions and variables of the unnamed namespaces become
`static`, types get a unique name in the component's namespace, files that use both styles end with one. No logic
changes; the diff is mostly indentation (one level less in the 53 nested ones), so it is reviewed with whitespace
hidden. At the end the check of phase 1 turns from a warning into an error.

### Phase 4: splits

One file per PR, each after its area has moved and its open PRs are merged:

1. `graphics_scene3d.cpp` into `scene/render/` and the camera commands into `scene/camera.cpp`.
2. `b3d.cpp` into the reader and `models/build.cpp`.
3. `runtime_system.c`, `process.c`, `system.cpp` into the files named in the layout.
4. `graphics_input.cpp`, `graphics_window.cpp`, `graphics_resources.cpp` (the lost-device part to `recovery.cpp`).
5. `collision.cpp` (the picking part to `picking.cpp`).
6. `code_compiler/source/main.cpp` into `driver/`.
7. `sound.c`, along the parts of the audio-effects design.

### Phase 5: shared helpers (refactors)

Not moves, so each gets the usual tests and, for the backends, a run on a physical machine:

1. The tools' copied helpers into `code_tools`.
2. The D3D11 and OpenGL call-list machinery into one shared file for immediate backends.
3. The three `create_resources` of gamma, HDR and SMAA, and the small byte helpers (`u16`, `put32`, ...) of the
   readers and writers.

### Phase 6: names and structures

After the moves and splits, one area per PR, because renames touch every line that uses a name:

1. One-letter and generic names in an area become words (rule 8). Mechanical, no logic change, but large: one area
   per PR, done with clang's rename tooling where it can be, so nothing is missed in macros or comments.
2. The big structures are regrouped (rule 9): `bb::gfx::state` first (cold, so only readability), then `bb::entity`
   with its per-class parts split out, which changes memory layout in hot loops and so gets numbers from a physical
   machine before it is ready, like any performance PR.

### Not in this plan

The performance findings (memcpy where an assignment would do, memcpy on unaligned data, loops that SSE2 and later do
in one instruction but LLVM can't vectorize because of possible side effects) belong to the optimization work, not to
the cleanup; Xaymar is passing them there. The cleanup PRs keep behaviour and speed the same, so they don't fix those,
and they don't make them harder to fix.

## Open questions

1. Is `static` + unique type names the rule Xaymar wants, or should file-local code go into a named namespace per file
   (`bb::gfx::d3d11_detail`) with the linkage cost described above?
2. Drop the area prefix inside folders (`gui/render.cpp`), or keep it (`gui/gui_render.cpp`)?
3. Rename `code_compiler/include` to `code_compiler/blitz_include`? It is visible in the installed tree only as
   `include/`, so the rename is source-only, but people who know the repository will look for it.
4. Group `tests/suite` into folders too, accepting renamed tests?
5. Keep the plan for 3.0, or start phase 1 and the conflict-free moves of phase 2 now, while the open PRs are few?
